mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.25% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent risk-aversion and reduced liquidity in the equity market.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the mean of the prior 30-day window (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS drops below 5.25% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a single month is associated with a short-term negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as market anticipates inflation cooling but equity valuations remain stretched.
failure_condition: Across 10 such episodes, the 60-day forward returns are not consistently negative (average p-value > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs per month for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as labor market strength supports equity risk appetite.
failure_condition: In regimes with high unemployment, the signal does not produce statistically significant positive 20-day forward returns (Granger causality p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 105 for two consecutive months, accompanied by a rise in retail sales proxy (HOUST), the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive due to stronger overall economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 105 AND HOUST > previous_month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: The interaction fails to predict positive returns in at least 70% of identified expansion phases (back-tested).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 10% in a month coincides with a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals weakening demand and potential supply-side shocks.
failure_condition: During non-shock periods, the signal does not produce a significant negative return (p-value > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for four consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which tends to drive positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns through optimism about growth and wage pressure.
failure_condition: The effect is not robust across different cycles (p-value of coefficient < 0.05 in OLS across all such episodes).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly retail activity (HOUST) falls by more than 5% from the prior month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to declining consumer confidence and spending.
failure_condition: The signal fails to predict negative returns in more than half of identified contraction regimes (walk-forward back-test).

mechanism_narrative: A one-time surprise cut in the federal funds rate by 0.25% produces a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as markets anticipate lower borrowing costs and easier financial conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < previous_month - 0.25% in a single month
failure_condition: Across 10 such surprise cuts, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p-value > 0.05).
